problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a technician to five remote field stations with the following geographic coordinates:

Station Alpha: (178, 56)
Station Beta: (11, 146)
Station Gamma: (162, 136)
Station Delta: (154, 174)
Station Epsilon: (18, 6)

The travel distances between stations, measured in kilometers, are precisely known from prior surveys:
Alpha to Gamma: 81.6 km
Alpha to Delta: 120.4 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 167.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 151.3 km
Beta to Delta: 145.7 km
Beta to Epsilon: 140.2 km
Gamma to Delta: 38.8 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 194.0 km
Delta to Epsilon: 216.1 km

Due to terrain restrictions, direct travel between Station Alpha and Station Beta is impossible. Furthermore, a routing protocol mandates that exactly one of two specific critical links must be incorporated into the circuit: either the connection between Station Beta and Station Gamma, or the connection between Station Gamma and Station Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-circuit inspection tour, wherein the technician visits each station exactly once before returning to the origin, thereby minimizing the total distance traveled.
